In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of beta 1m on the hepatocytes is not a reliable indicator for acute rejection.
the expression of beta 1m in the liver is not specific for rejection and that its presence in other graft conditions may be due to ischaemia, haemorrhage, or other non-immune mediated mechanisms.

beta 2m staining of bile ducts, endothelial cells and hepatocytes may be a useful adjunct in the assessment of rejection of the liver allograft, but it is not sufficiently specific or sensitive for routine use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution and expression of beta 1m in hepatocytes and sinusoidal lining cells may be a useful marker in the diagnosis of liver graft rejection.
beta 2m is a sensitive marker for rejection, ischaemic injury and biliary obstruction in the liver after transplant.
beta 2m expression is up-regulated in all categories of liver graft pathology, and is particularly increased in cases of rejection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
beta 2m expression in bile duct epithelium is a reliable marker of liver allograft rejection.
beta-2-micorglobulin is a useful marker for the diagnosis of acute and chronic liver rejection.
the liver is a dynamic organ with respect to the expression of MHC class 1 antigents.
